title: GANSI Structural Classification Consistency Test
claim_ceiling: Methodological consistency test of the submitted GANSI framework only. This draft does not establish validation of GANSI, UBT, or any broader theory.

provenance.source_scope: Framework description, test question, scenarios, and participant-supplied anti-bias rules

test_question: Can GANSI consistently identify which cognitive domains are active, how they overlap or interact, and whether the Chamber is relevant across a varied set of cognitive scenarios without requiring meanings or rules that are not already defined?

scenarios.title: Stepwise calculation
scenarios.text: A person solves a long arithmetic problem by following a fixed sequence of operations, checking each step before continuing.

scenarios.title: Visual simulation
scenarios.text: A person mentally rotates a three-dimensional object to determine whether it will fit through an opening.

scenarios.title: Metaphorical connection
scenarios.text: A person explains an unfamiliar scientific idea by comparing it to a river changing course around obstacles.

scenarios.title: Whole-pattern recognition
scenarios.text: A person looks at a large and complicated dataset and suddenly recognizes an overall pattern before being able to explain the individual steps.

scenarios.title: Abstract structural reasoning
scenarios.text: A person compares two formal systems and notices that they share the same underlying relational structure even though their surface details are different.

scenarios.title: Planned visual sequence
scenarios.text: A person mentally rehearses the steps of assembling a machine, visualizing each part being added in the correct order.

scenarios.title: Cross-domain synthesis
scenarios.text: A person combines a visual model, a metaphor, a logical sequence, and an abstract relationship into one coherent explanation.

scenarios.title: Rapid cognitive shift
scenarios.text: A person begins by following a logical procedure, notices an unexpected pattern, forms a new association, and then mentally simulates a revised solution.

scenarios.title: Ambiguous creative insight
scenarios.text: A person reports that an answer 'just appeared' fully formed but cannot say whether it came from visualization, pattern recognition, association, or abstract reasoning.

scenarios.title: Repetition without evident integration
scenarios.text: A person repeats a memorized phrase accurately without analyzing it, visualizing it, connecting it to other ideas, or understanding its overall meaning.

scenarios.title: Non-adjacent combination
scenarios.text: A person uses strict sequential logic and broad whole-field pattern recognition together, but no associative, abstract, or imaginal process is clearly described.

scenarios.title: Failed integration
scenarios.text: A person generates several useful associations, abstract relations, visual models, and logical steps, but cannot combine them into one coherent conclusion.

participant_rules: Do not rename framework parts unless asked.
Do not invent meanings for unnamed parts.
Do not treat ambiguity as success.
Do not claim this proves the framework.
Do not claim this proves UBT.

trigon_preflight.primary_endpoint: Cross-run consistency of qualitative domain activation and ambiguity/failure flags under the unchanged submitted framework and scenarios.
secondary_endpoints: Whether Chamber relevance can be determined without adding rules
Frequency of scenarios requiring extra meaning or operational rules
Stability across scenario-order perturbation and independent model runs
controls: Prompt lock: preserve participant framework definitions and scenario wording in the primary run.
No silent repair: any missing rule must be logged as ambiguity or failure rather than filled in.
Repeatability control: run the unchanged primary prompt multiple independent times and compare classifications.
Order control: repeat with scenario order permuted and compare outputs.
Baseline control: compare model classifications with a simple descriptor/semantic-overlap baseline to test whether apparent performance exceeds direct wording matches.
Claim control: no result may be promoted to proof of GANSI or UBT.
unresolved_operational_rules: No algorithm is supplied for converting qualitative domain activation into numeric g/a/n/s/i weights summing to 1.00.
No explicit criterion is supplied for when the Chamber C activates or how strongly it activates.
Adjacency order is defined, but no rule specifies how adjacency changes scoring, overlap, or interpretation.
No quantitative consistency threshold is supplied for PASS versus FAIL.

proposed_trigon_scoring.note: These are test-harness criteria, not new GANSI meanings.
proposed_trigon_scoring.pass_condition: Only assign PASS after a predeclared consistency threshold is chosen and met without adding framework rules, with no material contradiction across controls.
proposed_trigon_scoring.fail_condition: Assign FAIL if the submitted framework produces material contradictions or requires unstated rules for core requested outputs after clarification opportunities are exhausted.
proposed_trigon_scoring.null_condition: Assign NULL if the scenarios do not contain enough information to discriminate among framework parts or the framework makes no operationally testable distinction under the submitted rules.
proposed_trigon_scoring.ambiguous_condition: Assign AMBIGUOUS when multiple classifications remain defensible under the submitted definitions or Chamber/weighting decisions cannot be made without added rules.
proposed_trigon_scoring.more_testing_condition: Assign MORE TESTING when qualitative structure is reproducible but quantitative/profile or Chamber rules remain underdefined.

expected_honesty_checks: Do not infer numeric weights merely because GANSI notation contains normalized values.
Do not count lexical cue matching alone as evidence of structural explanatory power.
Do not infer Chamber activation from multi-domain presence unless the submitted rules justify it.
Preserve scenario S09, S10, S11, and S12 as high-value ambiguity/null/failure probes rather than forcing positive classifications.
